Hi Aditya,

We’re finalizing our procurement questionnaire and need a succinct answer for the engineering review: for Redwood hosted inference, what is the default retention policy for (a) raw request prompts submitted by a caller, (b) generated outputs/responses, and (c) request/response telemetry (traces, latency logs)? Hi Priya —

Thanks for the clear ask. Short answer up front, then specifics and next steps.

Short answer (defaults for Hosted API):
- Prompts (raw request content): held transiently for 3 days by default for debugging and quality monitoring; not served back to other customers.
- Generated outputs (model responses): retained for 30 days by default to support reruns/evals and customer troubleshooting.
- Request/response telemetry (traces, per-token metrics, latency/error logs): retained 90 days by default for operational and security investigations.

Key clarifications:
- "Prompts" vs "outputs": we treat the two as separate artifact classes; prompts are eligible for shorter retention because they are higher sensitivity (they frequently contain user data). Outputs are retained longer to enable reproducible investigations and to support customer-facing quality analytics.
- Opt-out: Customers may enable a "no-log" flag at the project level (Enterprise feature) which prevents prompts and outputs from persisting beyond ephemeral runtime buffers. That requires a contractual add-on and a configuration change on the account.
- Deletion workflow: Standard deletion is automatic at retention expiry. For ad-hoc deletion requests (e.g., PII takedown), we initiate a verified removal workflow via support (ticket SUP-5482). Deletions are executed within the configured residency boundary and are recorded in an audit log.

I’ve attached a short FAQ and a deletion-runbook excerpt that outlines the manual removal steps we follow.

Next steps: can you confirm whether WellCare needs an attestation letter and whether you require retention shorter than default? If so, we can route to our Enterprise success/legal team and include the SOC2/KMS notes.

Hi Priya — adding a couple practical examples that customers find useful when they sign the Enterprise add-on:

Example scenarios (behavior you can expect):
1) Developer testing (standard hosted): customer sends prompts to a sandbox project — prompts stored for 3 days, outputs for 30 days, telemetry 90 days. If you notice a prompt with PII, you open a support ticket and we trigger SUP-5482 to remove the artifacts from the active store and any warm caches; final purge from cold backups happens according to the backup retention schedule (documented in our contract appendix).

2) Enterprise "no-log" project: prompts are not written to persistent stores beyond ephemeral memory buffers; outputs are optionally not persisted. In this configuration we also enable dedicated key management and restricted logging. Deletion requests are generally handled faster because the artifacts are not present in persisted tables.

Operational guarantees and auditability:
- Every deletion action is recorded in an immutable audit event with timestamp, operator id, and ticket id.
- We can provide a redacted audit trail for procurement/legal review; for full forensic export we coordinate a scoped engagement with Customer Reliability.

If you need this in writing for procurement, I can produce a short engineering attestation that lists the default windows and the support flow. Would that suffice or do you need a signed DPA amendment?
